2014: 2014 has three location chapters: a four-month stay in Boston (Jan – May), a summer and winter break at NYU Shanghai, and NYU New York from late August onwards. Short trips in between: the Dominican Republic, New Hampshire, Providence, Macau and Istanbul.
2015: 2015 is structured around two Asia trips: a winter break in Shanghai and Hong Kong, and a summer run through Toronto, Taipei, Shanghai and Hong Kong. Between them, New York was the steady base (84% of plays).
2016: 2016 splits cleanly into two halves: a spring semester at NYU Florence, with March as the European-travel month (Iceland, Lisbon, Paris, Copenhagen; the Netherlands and Berlin in April), then New York from mid-May through year-end. Eight European countries in four months make it the most country-diverse year in the archive.
2017: 2017 is a heavily New York year (95% of plays), bookended by two Shanghai trips (January and December) and punctuated by a Morocco itinerary in March and a Coachella weekend in April.
2018: 2018 is the year of four real trips (Tulum, Paris, Mauritius and Madagascar, Barbados) around a steady New York base (88% of plays).
2019: 2019 is a New York year with a busy travel calendar: Coachella again, Italy, Marfa, Paris, and Seoul at Christmas.
2020: 2020 was a two-continent year, split 75% China / 23% New York, structured as two long Shanghai stays bracketing two New York stays. The January itinerary alone touched six countries before COVID grounded everything.
2021: 2021 is a two-act year split at June 16: five and a half months in Shanghai, then six and a half months back in New York. The second half stacks an unusually dense travel calendar: Joshua Tree and LA, upstate New York, London, Cologne, a Florida road trip, and Hong Kong en route to Shanghai for year-end.
2022: 2022 is a two-act year: a twelve-week winter stay in Shanghai (Jan 7 – Mar 27), then a return to New York, with autumn trips to Atlanta, Charlotte, Utah and Miami.
